papers.title: Planning over actions: Agentic reasoning for semi-structured table question answering
papers.authors: Huang J., Yun S., Chen S., Gu X., Shen B.
papers.abstract: Answering questions over semi-structured tables is fundamental to understanding real-world tabular documents, yet remains highly challenging. Irregular layouts — such as multi-level headers, merged cells, and heterogeneous regions — often induce semantic misalignment between questions and table contents. The task also requires multi-step compositional reasoning with cross-column dependencies, conditional logic, and numerical operations, where early errors can propagate. These difficulties are further amplified by domain-specific terminology and implicit conventions common in real-world tables.To address these challenges, we propose TQA-Agent, an agentic question answering framework for semi-structured tables. TQA-Agent formulates Table QA as an agentic search problem over an explicit action space of table actions. The framework involves LLM agents that dynamically explore, evaluate, and refine multiple candidate reasoning paths under complex table structures. An action set over tables is designed, which decomposes complex reasoning processes into interpretable and composable primitives with explicit intermediate states. TQA-Agent further incorporates a multi-agent collaboration mechanism, in which perception, planning, execution, evaluation, deliberation, and decision agents jointly generate, compare, and select reasoning paths through a trajectory-level deliberation process. This agentic reasoning strategy alleviates path dependency and effectively reduces error propagation in long reasoning chains, leading to more stable and reliable answers.We conduct extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets — CRT, TReB, SciTab, and SSTQA — covering diverse domains and varying table structures. Across datasets and backbone models, TQA-Agent consistently outperforms state-of-the-art LLM-based baselines. Using DeepSeek-V3, it improves average accuracy by 13.62, 11.71, 9.34, and 4.39 percentage points over Direct-Prompting, TableLLM, MACT, and ST-Raptor, respectively, and reaches 73.20% accuracy on the structurally complex TReB benchmark. Comparable gains are observed with GPT-4o, demonstrating robustness across backbone models. Further ablation studies reveal that the effectiveness of TQA-Agent comes from the coordinated interaction among diverse action categories, while the trajectory-level deliberation mechanism plays a critical role in enhancing reasoning robustness and overall answer quality.
